vulnerability.name: CVE-2024-42040
vulnerability.description: BOOTP vendor-area over-read in net/bootp.c bootp_handler() leaks 4 to 32 bytes of memory via crafted DHCP responses.

statements.impact_statement: net/bootp.c is built (CONFIG_CMD_BOOTP=y), but bootp_handler(), bootp_process_vendor() and bootp_process_vendor_field() are inside '#if !defined(CONFIG_CMD_DHCP)' (net/bootp.c lines 200-391) and CONFIG_CMD_DHCP=y, so they are preprocessed out; bootp_request() registers dhcp_handler() instead. CONFIG_SPL_NET is not set, so SPL has no network stack. Conditional: becomes affected if CONFIG_CMD_DHCP is disabled while CONFIG_CMD_BOOTP stays enabled; then backport upstream 81e5708cc2c8 (applies cleanly with git am, offset -17). Related, no CVE assigned: the compiled DHCP path has the same class of bug in dhcp_message_type(); upstream fixed it in f447887238822 (v2026.07), which is absent here and recommended as hardening.
statements.status_notes: Evidence level: source and .config analysis, confirmed on cross-built binaries of the BSP 7.8.0 tree (aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0, CONFIG_LTO=y; the build's .config is identical to the analysed one) using the link maps u-boot.map and u-boot-spl.map and the ELF symbol tables (readelf -s; 20,556 symbols in U-Boot proper, 3,906 in SPL). Under LTO a static function with one caller can be inlined, so the link map is the primary evidence and a missing symbol only supports it. net/bootp.o is linked into U-Boot proper, but its symbol table has dhcp_handler and no bootp_handler, bootp_process_vendor or bootp_process_vendor_field (dhcp_handler is the same kind of static, pointer-registered handler, so the absence is not an LTO artifact). The SPL link map has no net/bootp.o.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2024-57254
vulnerability.description: Integer overflow in squashfs sqfs_inode_size() symlink size calculation.

statements.impact_statement: The squashfs driver is not compiled into U-Boot proper or SPL: CONFIG_FS_SQUASHFS, CONFIG_SPL_FS_SQUASHFS and CONFIG_CMD_SQUASHFS are not set (fs/Makefile: obj-$(CONFIG_FS_SQUASHFS) += squashfs/; fs/squashfs/Makefile: obj-$(CONFIG_$(SPL_)FS_SQUASHFS)). sqfs_inode_size() (fs/squashfs/sqfs_inode.c) is in the source tree, unpatched, but not built. All four applied cleanly with git am on the BSP 7.8.0 tree; not build-tested.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2024-57256
vulnerability.description: Integer overflow in ext4fs_read_symlink() zalloc size leading to heap overwrite via a crafted ext4 filesystem.

statements.status_notes: ext4fs_read_symlink() (fs/ext4/ext4_common.c) is present, unpatched and compiled into U-Boot proper (CONFIG_FS_EXT4=y). It is reachable from the default autoboot: distro_bootcmd probes ext4 partitions on mmc 1 and mmc 2 and path lookup follows symlinks (ext4fs_find_file1()). Attacker needs write access to a probed ext4 filesystem (removable media, or local root in Linux). SPL is not affected: CONFIG_SPL_FS_EXT4 is not set. Evidence level: source and .config analysis, confirmed on cross-built binaries of the BSP 7.8.0 tree (aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0, CONFIG_LTO=y; the build's .config is identical to the analysed one) using the link maps u-boot.map and u-boot-spl.map and the ELF symbol tables (readelf -s; 20,556 symbols in U-Boot proper, 3,906 in SPL). Under LTO a static function with one caller can be inlined, so the link map is the primary evidence and a missing symbol only supports it. fs/ext4/ext4_common.o and four other fs/ext4 objects are linked into U-Boot proper and 39 ext4fs_* symbols are present; ext4fs_read_symlink() itself has no symbol because it is static with a single caller (ext4fs_find_file1()) and is inlined under LTO. The SPL link map has no fs/ext4 object.
statements.action_statement: Backport upstream 35f75d2a46e5 (the fix NVD lists) and also 107ed84602bb ('ext4: Fix zalloc()'), which NVD does not list. On this 64-bit target 35f75d2a46e5 alone is not enough: __builtin_add_overflow(u32, 1, &size_t) does not detect the wrap because 0x100000000 fits in a 64-bit size_t, so a 0xffffffff inode size becomes zalloc(0x100000000). That exceeds the 4 MiB heap (CONFIG_SYS_MALLOC_LEN=0x400000), memalign() returns NULL, and zalloc() in fs/ext4/ext4_common.h then runs memset(NULL, 0, 4 GiB) because it has no NULL check. 107ed84602bb switches to kzalloc(), which checks. Also apply the CVE-2024-57258 dlmalloc fixes. Both commits applied cleanly with git am on the BSP 7.8.0 tree; not build-tested, not runtime-tested. vulnerability.name: CVE-2024-57258
vulnerability.description: Integer overflows in dlmalloc request2size() and sbrk(), and x86_64 ptrdiff_t.

statements.status_notes: common/dlmalloc.c is always built into U-Boot proper (common/Makefile: obj-y += dlmalloc.o) and the request2size() and sbrk() flaws are present and unpatched. SPL is not affected: CONFIG_SPL_SYS_MALLOC_SIMPLE=y maps malloc to malloc_simple. The x86_64 ptrdiff_t part does not apply to arm64. The published trigger (squashfs) is not built, and no audit was done of whether a reachable caller can request a size near 2^63, so practical exploitability is rated low. The ruling is affected because the vulnerable code is present and the sigma-star advisory states other subsystems can reach it. Evidence level: source and .config analysis, confirmed on cross-built binaries of the BSP 7.8.0 tree (aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0, CONFIG_LTO=y; the build's .config is identical to the analysed one) using the link maps u-boot.map and u-boot-spl.map and the ELF symbol tables (readelf -s; 20,556 symbols in U-Boot proper, 3,906 in SPL). Under LTO a static function with one caller can be inlined, so the link map is the primary evidence and a missing symbol only supports it. U-Boot proper contains the full dlmalloc allocator (malloc 1,580 bytes, memalign, realloc, free, sbrk). The SPL image has none of malloc, memalign, realloc, free or sbrk, only a 64-byte calloc wrapper over malloc_simple; common/dlmalloc.o appears in the SPL link map only as an input with no allocator code linked.
statements.action_statement: Backport upstream 8642b2178d2c (request2size) then 0a10b49206a2 (sbrk). Also recommended: 9b9368b5c4dc ('dlmalloc: Make sure allocation size is within malloc area'), which closes the ~2^63 window. It rejects the CVE-2024-57256 0x100000000 request earlier, but zalloc() still needs 107ed84602bb. c17b2a05dd50 (x86_64 ptrdiff_t) is not needed on arm64. All applied cleanly with git am on the BSP 7.8.0 tree; not build-tested, not runtime-tested.

statements.impact_statement: net/tcp.c is not compiled: CONFIG_PROT_TCP, CONFIG_CMD_WGET (the only option that selects PROT_TCP) and CONFIG_TCP_FUNCTION_FASTBOOT are not set, and CONFIG_SPL_NET is not set. A module that boots normally from SD or eMMC never brings the network up. Attacker: adjacent network during that window.
